nodes.name: NVIDIA
nodes.summary: The Santa Clara GPU maker whose Hopper/Blackwell/Rubin data-center platforms define the AI accelerator market and the central subject of the share question. (grade A1)

nodes.name: AMD
nodes.summary: The Santa Clara chip designer whose Instinct MI-series GPUs are the leading non-NVIDIA merchant alternative for AI training and inference. (grade A2)

nodes.name: Intel
nodes.summary: The integrated US chipmaker whose Gaudi accelerators have struggled to gain AI share even as Intel Foundry seeks leading-edge relevance. (grade B2)

nodes.name: Broadcom
nodes.summary: The semiconductor and infrastructure-software giant that co-designs custom AI accelerators (XPUs) for Google, Meta, and others and supplies AI networking switch silicon. (grade A2)

nodes.name: Marvell
nodes.summary: The US fabless supplier of custom AI compute silicon, optical DSPs, and interconnect that competes with Broadcom for hyperscaler ASIC mandates. (grade B2)

nodes.name: TSMC
nodes.summary: The Taiwanese pure-play foundry that fabricates virtually all leading-edge AI accelerators (NVIDIA, AMD, Google, AWS) and controls CoWoS advanced packaging. (grade A1)

nodes.name: Samsung Foundry
nodes.summary: The foundry arm of Samsung Electronics seeking AI accelerator fab and packaging wins while its memory unit competes in HBM. (grade B2)

nodes.name: SK Hynix
nodes.summary: The South Korean memory maker that leads HBM3E supply and is the primary HBM partner to NVIDIA, a critical AI-accelerator bottleneck input. (grade A2)

nodes.name: Micron
nodes.summary: The US memory manufacturer scaling HBM3E/HBM4 to become a qualified third source alongside SK Hynix and Samsung for AI accelerators. (grade B1)

nodes.name: ASML
nodes.summary: The Dutch monopoly maker of EUV lithography systems without which no leading-edge AI accelerator can be manufactured. (grade A1)

nodes.name: Google
nodes.summary: The Alphabet cloud and AI company whose TPU is the most mature hyperscaler custom AI accelerator, used internally and offered via Google Cloud. (grade A2)

nodes.name: Amazon Web Services
nodes.summary: The Amazon cloud unit whose Trainium (training) and Inferentia (inference) chips, co-designed with Annapurna/Marvell, anchor its AI cost strategy. (grade A2)

nodes.name: Microsoft
nodes.summary: The Azure cloud and OpenAI-aligned hyperscaler developing the Maia AI accelerator to complement its massive NVIDIA and AMD GPU fleet. (grade A2)

nodes.name: Meta
nodes.summary: The social-media and AI company running one of the largest NVIDIA GPU fleets while deploying its in-house MTIA accelerators for recommendation and inference. (grade A2)

nodes.name: Oracle
nodes.summary: The enterprise software and OCI cloud provider scaling massive NVIDIA GPU clusters and tied to the OpenAI/Stargate compute buildout. (grade B1)

nodes.name: OpenAI
nodes.summary: The frontier AI lab behind ChatGPT whose enormous compute appetite shapes accelerator demand and which is co-designing custom silicon with Broadcom. (grade A2)

nodes.name: Anthropic
nodes.summary: The safety-focused frontier AI lab behind Claude that uniquely trains across Google TPU, AWS Trainium, and NVIDIA GPUs. (grade B1)

nodes.name: CoreWeave
nodes.summary: The specialized GPU cloud (neocloud) that buys and leases large NVIDIA fleets to AI labs and hyperscalers, deeply tied to NVIDIA and Microsoft. (grade B2)

nodes.name: Cerebras
nodes.summary: The wafer-scale AI chip startup whose CS-series systems target high-speed inference and HPC as an alternative to GPU clusters. (grade C2)

nodes.name: Groq
nodes.summary: The inference-focused startup whose LPU (language processing unit) targets ultra-low-latency token generation as a GPU alternative. (grade C2)

nodes.name: SambaNova
nodes.summary: The enterprise AI startup whose reconfigurable dataflow units (RDU) power full-stack inference and fine-tuning systems for governments and enterprises. (grade C3)

nodes.name: Cadence
nodes.summary: The electronic design automation vendor whose tools and IP are used by virtually all AI accelerator designers to tape out advanced chips. (grade B1)

nodes.name: Synopsys
nodes.summary: The EDA and semiconductor-IP leader whose tools, IP, and (post-Ansys) multiphysics enable AI accelerator tape-outs across the industry. (grade B1)

nodes.name: Arm
nodes.summary: The UK-based CPU architecture licensor whose IP underpins NVIDIA Grace, hyperscaler CPUs, and many custom AI SoCs. (grade B1)

nodes.name: Bureau of Industry and Security
nodes.summary: The US Commerce Department agency that administers export controls limiting China's access to advanced AI accelerators and semiconductor equipment. (grade A2)

nodes.name: China MIIT
nodes.summary: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, which steers industrial policy to build a self-sufficient domestic AI semiconductor supply chain. (grade B2)

nodes.name: SMIC
nodes.summary: China's largest foundry, fabricating Huawei Ascend and domestic AI chips on DUV-based 7nm-class processes under export-control constraints. (grade B2)

nodes.name: Huawei
nodes.summary: The Chinese technology giant whose HiSilicon Ascend AI accelerators are China's primary domestic alternative to restricted NVIDIA GPUs. (grade B2)

nodes.name: Jensen Huang
nodes.summary: The co-founder and CEO of NVIDIA whose strategy and public messaging shape the AI accelerator market's demand narrative. (grade A2)

nodes.name: Lisa Su
nodes.summary: The Chair and CEO of AMD whose roadmap and execution define the principal merchant challenge to NVIDIA's accelerator dominance. (grade A2)

nodes.name: SemiAnalysis
nodes.summary: The independent semiconductor research firm whose accelerator, packaging, and datacenter analysis is widely cited in share and supply debates. (grade B2)

nodes.name: TrendForce
nodes.summary: The Taiwan-based market-research firm whose HBM, DRAM, and AI-server forecasts are standard references for accelerator and memory market sizing. (grade B2)

nodes.name: Morgan Stanley
nodes.summary: The investment bank whose semiconductor research influences consensus estimates for NVIDIA share, custom-ASIC growth, and accelerator TAM. (grade B2)

nodes.name: xAI
nodes.summary: Elon Musk's frontier AI lab whose Colossus supercluster represents one of the largest single concentrations of NVIDIA GPUs for training. (grade B1)

nodes.name: Maia 100

nodes.name: MTIA

nodes.name: Grace CPU

nodes.name: inference market

nodes.name: Stargate
nodes.summary: The OpenAI/Oracle-led AI-infrastructure buildout escalating compute-buildout scale.

nodes.name: Project Rainier
nodes.summary: AWS's Trainium-based supercluster training Anthropic's frontier Claude models.

nodes.name: Colossus supercluster
nodes.summary: xAI's Memphis NVIDIA supercluster, among the largest single GPU concentrations.

nodes.name: EVT 2022-10 BIS first export controls
nodes.summary: BIS imposes first sweeping export controls restricting advanced AI GPUs and chipmaking tools to China, forcing NVIDIA to create cut-down China SKUs.

nodes.name: EVT 2023-08 NVIDIA H100 surge
nodes.summary: NVIDIA reports a data-center revenue surge as Hopper (H100) demand explodes, kicking off the AI accelerator boom.

nodes.name: EVT 2023-10 BIS tightens controls
nodes.summary: BIS tightens controls again, capturing NVIDIA's A800/H800 China parts and prompting the H20 redesign.

nodes.name: EVT 2023-11 Microsoft Maia unveiled
nodes.summary: Microsoft unveils its Maia 100 AI accelerator and Cobalt Arm CPU, signaling hyperscaler in-housing.

nodes.name: EVT 2023-12 AMD MI300X launch
nodes.summary: AMD launches Instinct MI300X, establishing the first credible merchant alternative to NVIDIA's data-center GPUs.

nodes.name: EVT 2024-03 NVIDIA Blackwell announce
nodes.summary: NVIDIA announces the Blackwell (GB200 NVL72) platform at GTC, extending its rack-scale and cadence lead.

nodes.name: EVT 2024-09 AWS-Anthropic deepen
nodes.summary: AWS and Anthropic deepen ties as Amazon commits additional billions and builds Trainium 'Project Rainier' training clusters.

nodes.name: EVT 2024-10 OpenAI-Broadcom chip
nodes.summary: Reports surface that OpenAI is co-designing a custom inference chip with Broadcom on TSMC, signaling lab-level vertical integration.

nodes.name: EVT 2024-12 BIS HBM controls
nodes.summary: BIS issues further controls on HBM and advanced tools to China, broadening the chokepoint campaign.

nodes.name: EVT 2025-01 Stargate announced
nodes.summary: OpenAI, Oracle, and partners announce the Stargate AI-infrastructure initiative, escalating compute-buildout scale.

nodes.name: EVT 2025-03 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra + Rubin tease
nodes.summary: NVIDIA details Blackwell Ultra (GB300) and teases Rubin (R100) on an annual cadence at GTC 2025.

nodes.name: EVT 2025-03 CoreWeave IPO
nodes.summary: CoreWeave completes its IPO, crystallizing the leveraged neocloud model built on NVIDIA allocation.

nodes.name: EVT 2025-04 BIS H20/MI308 license rule
nodes.summary: BIS effectively requires licenses for NVIDIA H20 and AMD MI308 China sales, materially curbing China accelerator revenue.

nodes.name: EVT 2025-06 AMD MI350/MI400 roadmap
nodes.summary: AMD unveils the MI350 series and the MI400/Helios rack-scale roadmap targeting NVIDIA at the system level.

nodes.name: EVT 2025-10 Broadcom 4th XPU customer
nodes.summary: Broadcom guidance and reports point to a fourth major custom-XPU customer (read as OpenAI), reinforcing the ASIC-shift thesis.

nodes.name: EVT 2026-03 GTC 2026 Rubin reaffirm
nodes.summary: At GTC 2026 NVIDIA reaffirms Rubin ramp timing and AI-factory demand, framing the market as still expanding faster than ASIC erosion.
